title: Unplaceable oversized piece is appended to a fresh batch without any size guard

finding.claim: Unplaceable oversized piece is appended to a fresh batch without any size guard
finding.evidence: When `_split_section` returns an unplaceable whole section, `_batch_sections_detailed` still does `current += piece` after only checking `if current and len(current) + len(piece) > max_chars`, so an oversized `piece` is accepted into an empty batch and exceeds the budget.
finding.recommendation: Before appending a piece, also handle the empty-batch case: if `len(piece) > max_chars`, mark batching incomplete and either return a dedicated failure path or keep the over-budget piece out of normal batches so downstream provider requests never exceed `max_chars`.

refutation.reason: The quoted line `current += piece` is inside the `for piece in pieces:` loop, which iterates over pieces already generated by `_split_section`. The oversize guard `if current and len(current) + len(piece) > max_chars` runs before this append, and `_split_section` already enforces that no individual

probe.summary: Oversize probe (`probes/oversize_probe.py`, result `oversize-6219e04d4c00.txt`): a section whose diff head alone is 179 chars at a 40-char budget is returned unplaceable by `_split_section`; `_batch_sections_detailed` sets incomplete=True; a full `run_review` is degraded with coverage.complete=False and the first gate reason stating 'section(s) could not be placed within the batch budget'. Contrast: a placeable oversized section batches entirely within budget with no content lost. Recorded honestly: the unplaceable batch actually sent is 209 chars — the section goes whole, flagged, never silently; in non-strict mode the gate can still pass while degraded.
